questions.text: What best describes your organisation?
questions.help: Determines baseline Data Fiduciary status.

questions.text: Do you offer goods or services to individuals in India (or process their data)?
questions.help: DPDP applies within India and extraterritorially to those serving Indian users (Act s.3).

questions.text: Which sector best fits your product?
questions.help: Some sectors carry extra obligations or exemptions.

questions.text: Roughly how many registered users do you have in India?
questions.help: Used only to check Third-Schedule class triggers (e-commerce/social >=2cr, gaming >=50L).

questions.text: Has the Central Government notified you as a Significant Data Fiduciary (SDF)?
questions.help: SDF duties (DPIA, audit, India DPO) apply ONLY to notified SDFs. Most startups are NOT SDFs.

questions.text: Are you a State or an instrumentality of the State?
questions.help: Certain State processing follows the Second Schedule standards (Rule 5).

questions.text: Do you operate as a registered Consent Manager?
questions.help: Consent Manager obligations (Rule 4) apply only if you act as one.

questions.text: Do you knowingly process personal data of children (under 18)?
questions.help: Triggers verifiable parental consent (Rule 10) + Act s.9 bans, subject to Fourth-Schedule exemptions.

questions.text: Do you process personal data of persons with disability who act through a lawful guardian?
questions.help: Triggers the s.9-proviso lawful-guardian consent path (DPDP-SEC9-GUARDIAN-001). Mirrors the children's-data gate; the guardian rule also fires when you process children's data.

questions.text: Do you transfer personal data outside India?
questions.help: Permitted subject to future Central-Govt restrictions (Rule 15).

questions.text: Which categories of personal data do you collect?
questions.help: Itemised personal data must be listed in your notice (Rule 3).

questions.text: Where does that data live?
questions.help: Used to map where personal data may reside (informs security & processor checks).

questions.text: Do you have a standalone, plain-language privacy notice?
questions.help: A separate, easy-to-read notice telling people what data you collect, why, and their rights (DPDP s.5 / Rule 3). Look for a 'Privacy Policy' / 'Privacy Notice' page linked in your website or app footer.

questions.text: How do you obtain consent?
questions.help: How users agree to your data use. 'Explicit opt-in' = an unticked box or clear action they must take. Check your sign-up / cookie / onboarding screens.

questions.text: Can users withdraw consent as easily as they gave it?
questions.help: A way for users to say 'stop using my data' that is as simple as giving consent was (DPDP s.6). Look for an account setting, an unsubscribe/opt-out link, or a documented request process.

questions.text: Do you have documented security safeguards (encryption, access control, logging)?
questions.help: Written technical/organisational measures protecting personal data — e.g. encryption, role-based access, audit logs (DPDP s.8(5) / Rule 6). Ask your engineering/security lead or check your security policy / SOC2-ISO docs.

questions.text: Do you have a personal-data-breach response process / register?
questions.help: A documented plan for what happens if data is exposed — who is told, and a log of incidents (DPDP s.8(6) / Rule 7 requires notifying the Board and affected people). Check for an incident-response runbook or breach register.

questions.text: Have you defined data retention and erasure periods?
questions.help: Rules for how long you keep personal data and when you delete it (DPDP s.8(7)-(8) / Rule 8). Check for a data-retention schedule or policy; if you 'keep everything forever', the answer is No.

questions.text: Do you publish a grievance/contact point for data questions?
questions.help: A named contact / channel users can reach about their data (DPDP s.13 requires a response within ~90 days). Look for a 'Grievance Officer', DPO email, or contact form in your privacy notice.

questions.text: What is the published grievance contact email?
questions.help: The email address you publish for data-protection questions and grievances. Find it in your privacy notice or website footer / contact page.

questions.text: Do you maintain an inventory of processors/vendors with data-processing contracts?
questions.help: A list of third parties that handle personal data on your behalf (AWS, analytics, CRM, payroll…) with data-processing agreements in place (DPDP s.8(2) / Rule 6(f)). Check your vendor list / DPA folder.

questions.text: Do you build, deploy, import, or distribute an AI system?
questions.help: Gates whether EU AI Act obligations apply at all.

questions.text: What is your role for that AI system?
questions.help: EU AI Act obligations are role-gated (provider duties differ from deployer duties).

questions.text: Are you the provider (you build/place the AI system), the deployer (you use it under your authority), or both?
questions.help: Drives which EU AI Act duties are shown: provider duties (Arts 9-22), deployer duties (Arts 26-27), or both.

questions.text: Is your organisation legally established in the EU?
questions.help: Non-EU providers placing high-risk AI on the EU market must appoint an EU authorised representative (Art. 22).

questions.text: Is the AI system placed on the EU market or is its output used in the EU?
questions.help: The EU AI Act applies extraterritorially when output is used in the EU (Art. 2).

questions.text: Is the AI model/system released under a free and open-source licence?
questions.help: Some EU AI Act duties carry open-source carve-outs (scope subject to legal review).

questions.text: Do you confirm your AI does NOT use any prohibited practice (Art. 5: manipulative/exploitative techniques, social scoring, untargeted scraping for facial DBs, etc.)?
Do you have an AI-literacy programme for staff operating AI systems (Art. 4)?
Do you disclose AI interaction and label AI-generated/deepfake content where required (Art. 50)?
Do you operate a documented risk-management system for the AI system (Art. 9)?
Do you have documented training/validation/test data governance (Art. 10)?
Do you maintain up-to-date technical documentation for the AI system (Art. 11)?
Does the system keep automatic logs / records over its lifecycle (Art. 18 & 20)?
Do you provide instructions-for-use / transparency information to deployers (Art. 13)?
Have you designed effective human-oversight measures (Art. 14)?
Do you have accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity measures (Art. 15)?
Do you operate a quality-management system (Art. 16)?
Have you classified whether the system is high-risk per Art. 6 / Annex III?
Have you completed (or planned) conformity assessment + CE marking (Art. 43)?
Is the system registered in the EU database where required (Art. 49)?
Do you operate a post-market monitoring system (Art. 72)?
(GPAI providers) Do you keep model documentation, a copyright policy and a training-content summary (Arts. 53-55)?
(Deployers) Do you use the system per instructions, assign human oversight, control input data, retain logs and notify workers (Art. 26)?
(Deployers) Have you completed a fundamental rights impact assessment where required (Art. 27)?
(Non-EU providers) Have you appointed an EU authorised representative by written mandate (Art. 22)?
Do you have a serious-incident reporting procedure to market surveillance authorities (Art. 73)?
